_comment: Sweep across a whole group (360x140, 14 frames): a wide swing arc, a stream, a mid cloud, a big end cloud and embers along the path. Built pointing right and mirrored for a caster on the right; scale it in the engine so the end cloud lands on the farthest target. Painted, outlined workbench recipe; vfx_workbench is free for subscribers, but export saves to the user's My effects.
_comment_prompt: /pixellab-pip run the vfx-wave-across-party blueprint for an ice spear, pale blue

TASK.instruction: Before the first call, require an explicit current-user request to run this blueprint, confirm an authenticated PixelLab MCP connection with vfx_workbench visible, and create the declared output directory empty (lowest free -2 suffix if taken). Resolve main colour ramp to six hex colours from near-black to highlight in the caster's own colours, taken from the project style (references/project-style.md) or the caster sprite; ask if neither gives one.
TASK.verify: The run is approved, vfx_workbench is callable, the ramp has six hex colours, and the output directory is new and empty.

MCP vfx_workbench.notes: Wave effect: {{effect description}}, caster facing {{caster facing | default: right}}.

TASK.instruction: With the step id returned by the immediately preceding call, call vfx_workbench with argv [<step id>, "render", <this task's render object as one JSON string>]. When the caster faces left, set recipe mirror to "x" (remove it when the template already mirrors and the caster faces right). One long stream reads as a pipe: after the first render, replace the single stream layer with three overlapping cartoon shape streams with staggered life [0.12,0.78], [0.19,0.84], [0.26,0.88]. Each change returns a new step id; patch with set, remove, add_layer or remove_layer ops and pass "frames" (1-based) to re-render only key frames 2, 5, 8 and 10. Then export with --name {{effect name}}. Save the exported GIF, sheet PNG and JSON unchanged as effect.gif, effect.png and effect.json.
TASK.verify: The peak frame is the largest and most solid, the last frames are mostly empty, the colours are the ramp's, nothing reads as a box or a pipe, and the saved files match the export.

TASK.instruction: The export's JSON gives every frame one flat time. Write timing.json with the per-frame durations {{frame durations | default: 100, 75, 75, 83, 83, 83, 92, 200, 100, 83, 79, 79, 79, 83 ms}} (anticipation, fast launch, a hold on the peak, fast break-up) for the engine's clip table; do not duplicate frames for timing.
TASK.verify: timing.json lists exactly 14 durations in frame order.
